tells: A single, specific idea: the world is a clockwork map, with cities that build themselves out of gears and cogs. Only this world could carry that idea, and it doubles as an orientation device for the viewer.
Real material and light: engraved metal on the astrolabe band, hand-carved wood, weathered parchment, a golden flare blowing out the highlights, and shallow depth of field across the miniatures.

Clear choreography: it opens on the astrolabe band, travels down to the map, watches the city mechanisms unfold, and closes back on the band for the logo lockup. The structure is a loop that pays off.
Credits are set in a classical engraved small-caps serif with a heraldic sigil bullet. They sit inside the 3D space, placed in relation to each set piece, and don't read as overlays.
Every frame is dense and layered, with foreground, midground and atmospheric background.
gaps: The credit type is quite small and low-contrast against busy detail in places (the Michelle Fairley card), so legibility could be pushed further.
The palette sits in a safe sepia/brass range. A sharper colour accent per region would strengthen the variety between locations.
The final logo lockup is more conventional than the body: a symmetrical flare-and-emblem reveal that could be more surprising.

tells: A coherent system built on extruded, layered '26' numerals that are re-skinned per nation with flags, crests and local ornament. It is a real broadcast toolkit, not a single layout.
Typographic variety with intent: heavy italic slab-sans for player and nation names, plus a Fraktur-adjacent condensed display for 'DIE NATIONALELF' wrapped in folk-ornament linework.
The frames change scale and camera (tunnel, player cutout with flag cloth, flat ornament plate, rotated 3D lettering), which suggests energetic, varied choreography.
Considered depth and lighting on the extrusions, with credible cloth simulation on the flag.
gaps: The idea is the expected sports-package formula (flag + number + player cutout). It lacks a single memorable concept on the level of A's clockwork map.
The player composite (Vinícius frame) is crowded and generic broadcast in feel. The cutout is stuck on rather than integrated with the world's light.
The material language is clean CG plastic. Adding real texture, grain or tactile surfaces would lift it above high-end broadcast norm.

tells: A witty, film-specific idea: every credit is a different fictional cigarette pack, so the subject's own packaging becomes the title sequence.
Typography with a strong point of view: each card uses a period-appropriate packaging face (script, Clarendon-ish serif, deco caps, condensed sans) that is pastiche done with expert specificity.
A deliberate mid-century print palette (cobalt, orange, cream, mint, signal red) with real paper and print texture, foil and misregistration-like warmth.
Tiny invented details reward attention: 'Underage sale prohibited', 'Honey-toasted tobacco lights', the tax stamp, the eagle crest.
gaps: The motion is largely camera moves over flat artwork. There is less physical choreography and depth than in A.
The framing is structurally similar card to card (close crop on a pack face), which risks repetition across the full length.
There is little light play. Specular foil glints or shifting real lighting on the packs would add the tactile depth seen in A.

defects: About 3 of the 4 seconds are static: per-second change drops to 0.4 and then 0.1. After the opening build, the only motion is a monospace line typing in.
All the movement happens in the first ~0.7s. 'SEASON 26' widens from condensed to extended (width axis), and the hero stack shifts slightly. Nothing moves after that, so there is no arc and no peak.
The info line uses a basic character-by-character typewriter reveal ('MATCHDAY 0' → '…19:4' → '…ES' → full). It has no cursor, rhythm or accent and reads as a template.
The hero 'NO DAYS OFF' is cropped hard against the left frame edge, and the 'O' of 'OFF' is cut off in the first frame. The crop reads as accidental, not as a deliberate full-bleed.
The hero type stays almost locked across the pairs. There is no overshoot, settle, follow-through or secondary motion on the main mark.
Outline 'SEASON 26' has a thin, slightly uneven stroke at 1:1. It sits on flat #0b0b0b with no grain, texture or light.
The small monospace line is very small and low-contrast at delivery size and is close to illegible.
gaps: Time and choreography: one 4s locked shot with a 0.7s move up front, against roughly 1s beats in top work. Missing are staged hand-offs (hero hits, then SEASON snaps wide, then info lands), a mid-piece build and a final accent or lock-up that resolves the motion.

Idea and type meaning: 'No Days Off' is never made physical. The type could refuse to rest, for example with constant motion, a looping relay or day-cycling counters. Instead it does a generic width tween and a typewriter, and the variable-width move carries no meaning.

Finish and material: flat black and one acid yellow with no texture, light falloff, motion blur or depth. The edge cropping of the hero and the thin outline stroke look unresolved rather than designed.
